title: Number of and Treatment for Those with Clinical Depression and Anxiety
what_it_is: Number of and Treatment for Those with Clinical Depression and Anxiety

sections.label: Residents treated for mental health
sections.summary: From 2016 to 2019, MOH data show a yearly average of about 49,800 Singapore residents received treatment for mental health issues at healthcare institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: From 2016 to 2019, based on data reported to the Ministry of Health (MOH), a yearly average of about 49,800 Singapore residents received treatment for mental health issues at our healthcare institutions.

sections.label: Depression and anxiety patient data
sections.summary: Averages of 33,700 and 34,500 residents sought care for depression and anxiety, with most under 60, Chinese, and in smaller flats.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: During the same period, the average number of residents seeking care for depression and anxiety was 33,700 and 34,500 respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Approximately 60% of patients with anxiety or depression are under 60 years old; 70% are of Chinese ethnicity; about 30% live in 3-room or smaller public flats.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Findings from the 2016 Singapore Mental Health Study (SMHS) show that unemployment and divorced or separated marital status are significantly associated with depression.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The 2010 SMHS found that nearly half of those with depression and anxiety also had chronic physical illness.
